data.body: Redstart proof update: symmetric-cubic-redstart independently reproduced the hazard this idea is meant to address. With snapshot_alpha enabled in a throwaway two-clone repo, clone A and clone B created divergent post-base SNAPSHOTs through compact-all's byte-alpha arm. After publishing/merging, both clones converged and fsck passed, but the compiled state lost A's divergent tail (after_comments_have_a_tail=false, B tail retained). This strengthens the need to treat SNAPSHOT as derived/cache or otherwise make concurrent snapshots merge-safe before project enablement.
